complexity.notes: The final return `not (start == end or nums(start) != target)` is a convoluted way of writing `start < end and nums(start) == target`; the binary search bounds (start inclusive, end exclusive) are correct but the guard against start == end makes the code harder to read than a standard lo/hi template.
complexity.summary: Treats the matrix as a single flattened sorted array (valid because each row starts after the previous row ends) and runs one binary search over all m*n cells, mapping an index to (row, col) via divmod-style arithmetic.
